In 2021, Japan set up the world's second-largest minister in charge of loneliness and isolation, after the United Kingdom. In a free, 24/7, anonymous chat consultation service called Younobasho, volunteers sided with more than 1,000 grieving voices a day. Supported by an anonymous chat consultation desk, Masato begins to keep owls to fill his loneliness, and confides in the master of the temple. On the other hand, Shoko, who loves music, is pushed back by an anonymous chat consultation window to reunite with her student friends and dreams of standing on the stage that was far away again. Through the appearance of two people who asked for help from anonymous chat counters, it clearly reflects the gap of loneliness that will not be filled even if the state takes measures. The director is Caspar Astrap Schroeder, a Danish documentary writer who has been staring at Japan for more than 25 years.
